title: Specs Guidelines Document Schema
description: What whoever uses a component or a foundation must observe, authored beside the spec as guidelines.yaml. The audience is a consumer, not a builder — what a builder must implement is supplemental.schema.json's subject. This document carries rules only: at a foundation's scope that means how tokens, themes and raw values are applied across the catalogue, never a per-token registry of what each token is for, which is tokens.schema.json's subject. An entry is a guideline item as the Design System Documentation Specification (DSDS) 0.23.1 defines one; the document is not a DSDS document, since DSDS requires kind and for on every section and this carries neither, so an exporter wraps a concern's entries in a DSDS section. Three scopes share this shape, and entries across scopes are additive rather than overriding (DSPEC-56). This file is self-contained. (ADR-118)

anatomy.description: Rules about the element tree: what parts a component has and how they nest.

props.description: Rules about the props a component takes, and what a caller may pass.

styles.description: Rules about the style values a component's parts carry, and how a foundation's values are applied.

slotComposition.description: Rules about what may fill a slot, in what quantity, and in what arrangement.

events.description: Rules about what a component emits, and when.

accessibility.description: Rules about what assistive technology receives, and what a caller must supply for it.

behavior.description: Rules about what a component does in response to interaction or state.

motion.description: Rules about how a component traverses a change rather than where it ends up.

layout.description: Rules about how a component's parts are arranged and sized relative to each other.

overrides.description: Rules about what a caller may replace or supply in place of a component's own part.

naming.description: Rules about why a component, prop, or part carries the name it does.

GuidelinesMeta.description: Authorship and review status for the document as a whole. Every member is optional; status is the member that earns the block, because it is how a ratifier knows whether they are reading a proposal or settled guidance.

concern.description: The subject this document covers, restating what the containing directory names — a foundation concern at the foundation scope, a component name at the component scope.

status.description: Where the document sits in its review cycle.

oneOf.description: Drafted and awaiting a ratifier; its rules are not yet the system's position.
Reviewed and adopted; its rules are the system's position.
Superseded or withdrawn; kept for the record and not to be followed.

author.description: Who authored it. Duplicates git history, and is here for a reader who will not consult git.

updated.description: When it was last revised, as YYYY-MM-DD. Hand-maintained, so it can go stale.

sources.description: The generated reports this document was synthesized from, as workspace-relative paths.

ObligationLevel.description: How strongly a guideline binds, with RFC 2119 semantics. DSDS 0.23.1 defines the first four; may is RFC 2119's fifth and is added here, because a permission recorded as should asserts an obligation the system does not hold. Each description names the colloquial words an author reaches for, because the authored files already use them.

oneOf.description: An absolute requirement; a usage that disregards it is wrong. Often written instead as required, or always.
A strong recommendation; disregard it only with a considered reason. Often written instead as recommended, or prefer.
A strong recommendation against; do it only with a considered reason. Often written instead as avoid.
An absolute prohibition; a usage that does it is wrong. Often written instead as never.
A permission the system grants, and neither requires nor discourages. Often written instead as optional, or could.

GuidelinesCheckedBy.description: How a guideline is checked. The checks member names what does the checking, and is required whenever this is automated.

oneOf.description: A test or lint rule decides it, with no human reading required.
A tool surfaces candidates and a human judges them.
A human decides it, with no tool involved.

GuidelineReference.description: A reference to one thing, either inside this workspace or outside it. Exactly one member is present: to names something the workspace holds, href names something it does not. Resolution of to is DSPEC-57.

to.description: What this points at inside the workspace — a component, a token, or an item within one.

href.description: What this points at outside the workspace, as an absolute URL.

GuidelineReferences.description: One or more references to things, inside this workspace or outside it.

Section.description: Rules for one concern a consumer must observe.

GuidelineEntry.description: One rule a consumer must observe.

statement.description: The rule itself, as a sentence a reader can act on.

alternatives.description: What to use instead, when the remedy is a thing this can point at. Preferred over instead whenever the remedy can be named, because a pointer resolves and a sentence does not.

instead.description: What to do instead, when the remedy is a rule rather than a thing. An exporter folds this into statement rather than dropping it (DSPEC-59).

refines.description: A broader guideline this one elaborates.

checks.description: What does the checking. Required when checkedBy is automated.
